title: Nvidia-backed Iambic Therapeutics launches IPO as biotechs buck market gloom
source_used: Reuters, read on SRN News and AOL.ca wire copies (reuters.com returns 401)
key_facts: Nvidia-backed Iambic Therapeutics, which uses AI to develop drugs, aims to raise up to $159.4 million in its US IPO (Reuters, 8 Oct 2026).
The IPO would value it at up to $805.8 million, per a regulatory filing on Tuesday.
About 9.38 million shares are offered at $15 to $17; ARK Investment Management and Duquesne Family Office indicated interest in $60 million worth.
Founded in 2019 as Entos; it advances drug candidates for solid tumors and has partnerships with AbbVie and Takeda.
An IPOX analyst called it a clinical-stage biotech with an AI-enhanced platform, not a pure AI play.
It plans to list on the Nasdaq under "IAM"; lead underwriters are J.P.Morgan, Jefferies, BofA Securities and Citigroup.
The fall IPO market has been hit by delays as Treasury yields and volatility make investors cautious.
quote_evidence: Nvidia-backed Iambic Therapeutics, which uses AI to develop drugs, is aiming to raise up to $159.4 million in its US IPO, as the biotech sector emerges as a bright spot in an otherwise lackluster market.
Iambic is marketing roughly 9.38 million shares at $15 to $17 apiece.
A successful listing would set Iambic apart in a fall IPO market hit by a string of delays as rising Treasury yields and market volatility make investors more cautious.
why_it_matters_hint: An AI drug company is testing public-market appetite while other listings are delayed.
